title: Circularity-Adjusted Evaluation Record
purpose: Extend conventional economic evaluation with environmental, material, residual-value, resilience, equity, rebound, and burden evidence.
notes: Synthetic example. Replace all values with authorized local evidence before institutional use.

records.Guidance: Define the service delivered, population, quality level, volume, and time horizon.
records.Institutional response: Compare edge and cloud diagnostic AI per 1,000 quality-assured examinations over five years.

records.Guidance: Specify model, data, compute, network, devices, supporting equipment, maintenance, replacement, transport, and disposition included.
records.Institutional response: Model, data transfer, compute, storage, network, edge hardware, cooling, maintenance, replacement, transport, and disposition.

records.Guidance: Report health, service, workforce, quality, and economic outcomes before circular adjustments.
records.Institutional response: Report diagnostic outcomes, turnaround, staff time, downtime, integration, monitoring, and five-year cost.

records.Guidance: Report energy, water, carbon, virgin and recovered material, waste, and critical dependencies per functional unit.
records.Institutional response: Report kWh, water, kg CO2e, hardware mass, critical materials, and waste per 1,000 examinations.

records.Guidance: Record useful remaining life, resale, redeployment, take-back, recovery credit, and realization cost.
records.Institutional response: Record redeployment value, take-back credit, secure-erasure cost, and verified recovery.

records.Guidance: Record redundancy, availability, lead time, dependency, repair capacity, and continuity effects.
records.Institutional response: Assess connectivity dependence, fallback, repair lead time, parts, and continuity.

records.Guidance: Identify who benefits, who bears environmental and labor burdens, and which regions or groups are affected.
records.Institutional response: Assess access and geographic distribution of energy, water, labor, and end-of-life burden.

records.Guidance: Explain which effects are monetized, which remain disaggregated, valuation sources, and overlap with conventional costs or outcomes.
records.Institutional response: Monetize verified energy and carbon only; report other effects separately; avoid duplicate residual value.

records.Guidance: Test use, lifetime, performance, prices, disposal, recovery, environmental factors, and induced demand.
records.Institutional response: Test utilization, model size, hardware life, cloud price, energy mix, recovery rate, and induced demand.

records.Guidance: State conventional and adjusted results, non-compensatory constraints, preferred option, conditions, and review triggers.
records.Institutional response: Prefer robust total value subject to safety, security, continuity, equity, and verified disposition safeguards.
